data.title: 1st Summit Bancorp of Johnstown Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
1st Summit Bancorp of Johnstown, Inc. (OTCID: FSMK) (the “Company”), parent company of 1st Summit Bank, today announced net income of $2.55 million for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 2.3% compared to $2.49 million for the second quarter of 2026 and 49.7% compared to $1.70 million for the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the first nine months of 2026 totaled $7.3 million.

Third quarter results are a continuation of the progress established earlier in the year, with strong loan growth, further expansion in net interest margin, and stable credit quality. Net interest income increased 3.4% from the prior quarter, while noninterest expense increased just 0.6%, demonstrating continued discipline as the Company grows and invests in its future.

“Our third quarter results reflect the work that we have put into strengthening 1st Summit,” said Allison Johnson, Chief Executive Officer of 1st Summit Bancorp. “During the third quarter, we grew loans at a double-digit annualized rate, maintained stable credit quality, and kept quarterly expense growth below 1%. We are particularly encouraged by our ability to grow the loan portfolio while also maintaining the strong underwriting standards that have served this Bank well.”

She continued, “The progress is visible in our results, but it begins with our people and the relationships they build every day. Our team has remained focused on understanding customers’ needs, earning their business, and managing the Bank with discipline. We believe that this commitment will continue to help us build a stronger earnings foundation while creating room to invest in the customer experience and the future of the franchise.”

Balance Sheet Growth

Gross loans increased $24.2 million during the quarter to $941.5 million at September 30, 2026, representing annualized growth of 10.47%. Loans increased $60.2 million, or 9.1% annualized, from December 31, 2025. Quarterly loan growth was led by commercial real estate and construction, land and development lending.

Total deposits increased $13.9 million to $1.19 billion at September 30, 2026, representing annualized growth of 4.68%. Growth in interest-bearing demand deposits more than offset declines in time deposits and noninterest-bearing deposits during the third quarter of 2026. The loan-to-deposit ratio increased to 79.1% at September 30, 2026, compared to approximately 78.0% at June 30, 2026, as the Company continued to improve its earning asset mix.

Management continues to view loan growth and the development of lasting deposit relationships as closely connected priorities, and that growing those relationships supports the Bank’s lending capacity and strengthens the funding foundation needed to sustain its progress.

Total assets were $1.52 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.53 billion at June 30, 2026. Shareholders’ equity totaled $99.5 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $109.9 million at June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a $12.1 million increase in accumulated other comprehensive losses. Changes in accumulated other comprehensive income are recorded within shareholders’ equity rather than current-period net income.

Net Interest Margin and Profitability

Net interest income totaled $9.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $316 thousand, or 3.4%, from the second quarter of 2026 and an increase of $1.5 million, or 19.1%, from the third quarter of 2025. Loan interest income increased $545 thousand from the prior quarter, more than offsetting lower investment income and higher total interest expense.

Net interest margin expanded to 2.63% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 2.57% for the second quarter of 2026 and 2.28% for the third quarter of 2025. The improvement reflects continued progress in shifting the earning asset mix toward loans and strengthening the Company’s underlying earnings capacity.

With the current interest rate environment and liability mix, the pace of further margin expansion will depend increasingly on continued loan growth in the fourth quarter. Management remains focused on disciplined loan pricing and developing deposit relationships that support sustainable growth.

Profitability and operating efficiency remained solid during the third quarter of 2026:

  • Annualized return on average assets was 0.66%.

  • Annualized return on average equity was 9.47%.

  • The efficiency ratio remained essentially stable at 73.64%, compared to 73.61% for the second quarter of 2026.

Credit Quality Remains Stable

Credit quality remained stable during the third quarter of 2026 as the loan portfolio grew. Nonaccrual loans represented 0.32% of total loans at September 30, 2026. The allowance for credit losses totaled $7.3 million at September 30, 2026, or 0.78% of gross loans, and covered nonaccrual loans by approximately 2.39 times. The provision for credit losses was $200 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026, unchanged from the prior quarter.

Management believes this performance reinforces the value of consistent underwriting and active portfolio monitoring, and that preserving credit quality remains central to the Company’s approach to growth and its ability to translate new business into lasting shareholder value.

Noninterest Income and Expense

Noninterest income totaled $2.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decline of $251 thousand, or 10.9%, from the second quarter of 2026, primarily reflecting lower interchange and wealth management income. Compared to the third quarter of 2025, noninterest income increased 2.9%. No gains on sales of investment securities were recognized during the quarter.

Noninterest expense totaled $8.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $51 thousand, or 0.6%, from the second quarter of 2026. Lower professional services and other operating expenses helped offset increases in salaries and benefits, data processing, and regulatory assessments and insurance.

The Company continues to manage everyday operating costs carefully while directing resources toward investments that improve service and support future growth.

Looking Forward

“We enter the final quarter of 2026 encouraged by what our team has accomplished and focused on closing out a strong year by delivering solid operating results,” Johnson concluded. “Our priorities remain clear: continue growing quality loans, build lasting deposit relationships, and preserve the discipline behind our progress. We are proud of how far we have come and remain committed to doing the work that creates long-term value for our shareholders, customers, and communities.”

About 1st Summit Bancorp of Johnstown, Inc.

1st Summit, through its wholly owned subsidiary, 1st Summit Bank (the “Bank”), is a community oriented financial institution that primarily focuses on relationship banking for both consumers and businesses. From 17 full-service community offices and one loan production office, the Bank provides a full array of personal and business banking solutions, investment management and trust services. The Bank serves communities throughout the counties of Cambria, Westmoreland, Blair, Somerset, and Indiana. Please visit Home | 1st Summit Bank for more information.

data.title: ASND Shares Shrug Off Positive European Opinion For FDA-Approved Achondroplasia Drug
data.description:
Key points:
  • Final European Commission authorization is still pending, with a decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a potential first launch in Germany in the first quarter of 2027.
  • Ascendis has three approved commercial products.
  • TransCon CNP, marketed as YUVIWEL in the U.S., received FDA approval in February 2026.

Ascendis Pharma (ASND) said on Friday that it has received a positive European regulatory opinion for its once-weekly treatment for children with achondroplasia.

Shares of the company closed down 0.6%, as investors likely viewed the positive opinion as expected, provided it is already approved in the U.S. TransCon CNP, marketed as YUVIWEL in the U.S., received FDA approval in February 2026 to increase linear growth in children two years and older with open growth plates.

CHMP Opinion On Ascendis Drug

Ascendis said the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use adopted a positive opinion on Ascendis’s application seeking approval for the drug in achondroplasia for children two years of age and older whose epiphyses, or the expanded end of a long bone, are not closed.

The opinion followed review of data from three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials plus up to three years of open-label extension results, including the pivotal ApproaCH trial. Final European Commission authorization is still pending, with a decision expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a potential first launch in Germany in the first quarter of 2027.

Chief Executive Officer Jan Mikkelsen said the positive opinion reflects the unique profile of TransCon CNP and that the therapy remains a foundational product in the company’s growth disorder portfolio supporting its longer-term objectives.

Ascendis has three approved commercial products, including TransCon CNP. In the second quarter, or its first quarter of commercial sales, the drug recorded €7.6–8 million in revenue, accounting for a small portion of the company’s overall product revenue of €315 million. YORVIPATH accounts for a lion’s share of the company’s overall sales.

How Did ASND Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ASND stock stayed within bearish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed within normal levels.

ASND stock has gained 6% year-to-date.

More storage sold helps shareholders most when pricing and investment spending leave plenty of cash behind.

data.title: Wall Street ends down sharply, worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Chips, AI infrastructure companies fall as debt concerns linger
  • S&P 500 and Nasdaq suffer steepest weekly losses since June
  • Tesla dips after unveiling electric sports car
  • S&P 500 -1.09%, Nasdaq -2.15%, Dow -0.34%

By Noel Randewich

Wall Street ended sharply lower on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.

The Nasdaq extended losses from earlier in the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Broadcom fell 4.5%, and the PHLX chip index sank 3.8% in its eighth straight day of declines, its longest losing streak since 2008.

Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries.

"There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in ​Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk."

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The S&P 500 declined 1.09% to end the session at 7,659.44 points.

The Nasdaq declined 2.15% to 26,140.03 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.34% to 52,002.41 points.

Reflecting a rotation from tech stocks into other areas of the stock market, six of the S&P 500's 11 sector indexes rose, led by energy , up 2.47%, followed by a 1.4% gain in utilities .

Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 18.6 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.7 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell almost 1.95% and the Nasdaq slumped 4.48%, their deepest weekly declines since June. The Dow climbed 0.67% for the week.

Third-quarter earnings season shifts into high gear next week with reports from Tesla , Meta Platforms and Procter & Gamble . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging more than 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data.

While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2026.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday voiced optimism about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January.

Tesla dropped 3.1% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares dipped 2.8%.

Declining stocks roughly matched rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX)..

The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 51 new highs and 353 new lows.

Apple shares climbed 1% on Friday morning as delivery estimates for its first foldable smartphone slipped into late January, signaling an early supply crunch ahead of the device's retail launch.

The iPhone Duo, priced from $1,999, opens for retail sales Oct. 23. Apple's U.S. online store lists Jan. 29 as the estimated delivery date for models with 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB of storage.

The extended wait comes as Apple looks to expand its premium smartphone lineup with a foldable design. Counterpoint Research estimates the company could sell six million Duo units in 2026. The device features two batteries, a glare-reducing screen finish and a 48-megapixel Fusion camera.

Demand has also supported Apple's latest conventional models. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max recorded 12% year-over-year growth during their first week in China, helping the company capture 33% of the country's smartphone market for the period, according to Counterpoint.

Apple recently joined Nvidia as the second company to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization. The company's standard iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2 and iPhone 18e are expected to arrive around March 2027.

data.title: Illinois American Water Announces 2026 "Water Keeps Life Flowing" Art Contest
data.description:
Grade school contest raises awareness of the role high-quality water systems play in students' daily lives

BELLEVILLE, Ill., Oct 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Illinois American Water encourages students to showcase their creativity by submitting artwork to the company's "Water Keeps Life Flowing" art contest. Entries from 3rd, 4th, and 5th grade students will capture what high-quality water service means to them, and artwork will be accepted through Friday, Nov. 13, 2026.

"Our annual art contest encourages students to bring art and science together to depict the importance of water in a creative way," says Brian Eisenloeffel, President, Illinois American Water. "We are excited to see what safe, clean, and reliable water means to our young customers."

Art contest entries open Oct. 16, 2026, just one day after the annual observance of the U.S. Water Alliance's Imagine a Day Without Water on Oct. 15, which encourages people to consider the devastating impact of a single day without access to safe, clean water.

Eisenloeffel added, "Water keeps our lives flowing by helping families, schools, communities, and the environment thrive. Water is essential for drinking, cooking, growing gardens, protecting public health, supporting local businesses, and helping firefighters keep our communities safe. Illinois American Water plays a critical role in customers' daily lives by providing water service that supports these essential activities and community operations."

Up to 10 winners will earn a prize pack, valued at roughly $100, to share with their classroom. Available prize packs include:

  • Creative Kids – art supplies like colored pencils, markers, crayons;
  • STEM Education – science trivia board game, magnetic tiles, Guess in 10 Animal Planet; and
  • Classroom Party – Uno Junior, 30 Fidget Toy Keychains, Would You Rather? School & Classroom Edition.

The winning artwork may be featured in future Illinois American Water customer communications. Past winning artwork can be found on the company's Facebook page: @ilamwater.

Additional contest rules and guidelines can be found on Illinois American Water's website under the News & Community tab.

About American Water

American Water () is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Illinois American Water

Illinois American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 600 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 1.3 million people. American Water also operates a quality control and research laboratory in Belleville.

data.title: Alcon Gets FDA Approval for Brytly Eye Drops
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Alcon received approval from the Food and Drug Administration for its Brytly eye drops.

data.title: JPMorgan Stocks Rise After Buy Upgrade as Credit Costs Face Scrutiny
data.description:
Banking giant JPMorgan Chase rose to $341.75, up approximately 1.85%, at 11:17 a.m. ET on October 16, following a valuation-driven upgrade. According to The Fly, Freedom Broker lifted its rating to Buy from Hold on October 15 and nudged its price target to $370 from $365. Its reasoning was straightforward: the entry price had become more attractive.

Credit costs still deserve a close look. JPMorgan's October 13 earnings release reported a $539 million net reserve addition and $2.2 billion in net charge-offs during the third quarter, bringing total credit costs to roughly $2.7 billion. The standardized common-equity Tier 1 capital ratio stood at 13.9%. The reserve addition increased the cushion for potential losses; charge-offs reflected losses already recognized.

The valuation picture adds a wrinkle: shares trade 10.26% above the $309.94 GF Value estimate, suggesting the upgrade does not automatically make the stock a bargain. The reserve build accounted for roughly one-fifth of quarterly credit costs. The next test is whether lending returns can hold up without a sharper rise in provisions or actual losses. A higher price target helps sentiment. Sustained earnings need credit quality to cooperate.

data.title: Short Sellers Have Earned $32B Over The Past Week Amid Chipmaker Selloff: Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bearish investors accumulated roughly $32 billion in paper profits over seven days as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped over 12% during an eight-session slump. 
  • Broad market indexes felt the ripple effect, with the S&P 500 on track for its worst weekly decline since June and the Nasdaq 100 sliding 5%. 
  • Short sellers betting against AI cloud provider CoreWeave Inc. netted more than $1 billion in mark-to-market profits following distressed debt signals and rising default risks. 

Short sellers have bagged a multi-billion-dollar payday amid a retreat in semiconductor stocks driven by CoreWeave’s debt concerns.

Short sellers recorded $32 billion in gross paper profits over a seven-day span as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeted more than 12%, S3 data showed, as quoted by Bloomberg.

The sector benchmark, widely known as the SOX, extended its slump to eight consecutive trading days on Friday, putting it on pace to mirror its longest losing streak since 2006.

Market Anxiety Around AI Spending Persist 

The recent decline reflects growing market anxiety about elevated interest rates, lofty tech valuations, and the massive AI capital expenditures.

The selloff in chips has spilled over into broader equity benchmarks, setting the S&P 500 up for a 1.7% weekly decline, its steepest since June, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropped 5% in the week ending October 16.

Out of the 30 companies comprising the SOX index, 20 have lost over 10% of their value since the downturn began. Coherent Corp.(COHR) led the losses with a dive of nearly 30%.

"The run up in chips was very aggressive so invariably there was going to be some consolidation or pull back," Dec Mullarkey of SLC Management told Bloomberg.

CoreWeave Shorts Yield Massive Returns

Short sellers targeting CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV), an AI-focused cloud computing firm, logged over $1 billion in gains as the company's equity dropped more than 20% over the week.

CoreWeave's debt instruments slipped into distressed territory, with credit-default swaps indicating a greater than 50% likelihood of default over the next five years.S3 data noted that a portion of the short interest in CoreWeave stems from convertible bond arbitrage strategies rather than purely directional bearish bets.

"CoreWeave specifically is going to need a new story," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager of the Rational Equity Armor Fund told Bloomberg. "It's going to need time to digest this new reality."

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) dropped 1.2%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) eased 0.5%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) fell 2.5% on Friday.

data.title: Tesla Has Built a Flying Car. It Will Blow Your Mind. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

OK, that was cool. And Tesla CEO Elon Musk wasn't wrong: People might not have believed it if they hadn't seen it with their own eyes.

Tesla unveiled the latest version of its long-awaited Roadster on Thursday evening. The event promised to be mind-blowing, and it was — the car flies. It flies. The Roadster event wasn't enough to boost Tesla stock on Friday.

Shares of the electric-vehicle — and flying car — company fell Friday by 2.1% to $354.72. The S&P 500 dropped 1% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.3, while the Nasdaq Composite stumbled by 2%.

The demonstration started with the car driving up a curved wall. Eventually, it was upside down. Then, it jumped off the wall, flipped over, and landed softly. Later, the car jumped over Tesla's vehicle lineup while spinning in the air.

It's a little difficult to describe. The car uses a vacuum to suction it to the ground. That will improve driving performance. Tesla said the car can turn a corner pulling two Gs (two times the normal force of gravity).

As for flying, the car uses thruster technology adapted from SpaceX. Ten nozzles manage 250 kilograms of air stored in special high-pressure tanks. The air tanks can recharge themselves; no special refueling equipment is needed.

The air thrusters also helped the car go from zero to 60 mph in 0.8 second.

The new Roadster was teased in 2017, almost a decade ago. It follows the first Roadster, Tesla's first car, which started selling in 2008 and was built on a Lotus platform.

Back then, the odds that Tesla would be a viable car company looked vanishingly small. That's obviously no longer the case. Tesla is the world's most valuable car company by a lot.

To be sure, Barron's didn't see a large chance of a big stock move. There is a limited market for supercars costing hundreds of thousands of dollars. Still, the car drove upside down and hopped over other cars.

Exactly what the car will cost isn't known yet. Production is planned for 2028. There will be three versions: a base model, a thruster-enhanced model, and a rocket model. The rocket version is "invite only." It's the version that can essentially fly. The thruster version will go from zero to 60 mph in under a second. The base model is a very expensive EV.

The event was also light on traditional EV specs. Battleroad research analyst Ben Rose was expecting a four-seater. The car has only two seats.

The Roadster is definitely cool, and a unique engineering achievement. All-In podcast host Jason Calacanis said recently that the event would "blow people's minds."

He wasn't wrong. Still, Tesla shares are all about AI now, with investors looking to AI-trained robo-taxis and humanoid robots for future earnings growth. (Musk said the Roadster would eventually be the last manually driven car Tesla made).

The event's lasting impact may be stronger ties between Tesla and SpaceX. Many investors and Wall Street analysts expect the two companies to merge one day, consolidating Musk's AI effort under one corporate roof.

The Roadster collaboration is the latest example of the two companies working together. They also collaborate on AI agents, semiconductor manufacturing, and power supply, among other things.

data.title: ASSA ABLOY sells PKI business unit to Vista Equity Partners

STOCKHOLM, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ASSA ABLOY has signed an agreement to sell HID's PKI business unit to Vista Equity Partners ("Vista").

The PKI business unit (Public Key Infrastructure) provides digital trust, identity, authentication, encryption, and certificate management solutions. The business unit includes PKI SaaS - IdenTrust and HydrantID - credential management, and ZeroSSL.

"I find it very satisfying that with Vista, the PKI business unit and its employees and customers gain a committed long-term investor, creating new opportunities for the future and I wish them every success," says Nico Delvaux, President and CEO of ASSA ABLOY.

"Our PKI team has built a strong business with a strong customer base, and Vista has the expertise to take it forward as the market evolves," says Björn Lidefelt, EVP and Head of HID. "We are pleased with this outcome for our customers, our employees, and for HID."

The divested business had sales in 2025 of MUSD 58 (approx. MSEK 570) with a strong operating margin.

The divestiture is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close during the fourth quarter of 2026.
